name: Complete Sports and Management India Limited

debate.name: Complete Sports and Management India Limited

rounds.text: Complete Sports and Management India Limited trades at a reasonable P/E of 18.4x [E1] while exhibiting extraordinary capital efficiency, boasting an exceptional ROCE of 63.92% and an ROE of 54.03% that vastly outperform sector benchmarks of 7.84% and 6.79% respectively [E10, E9]. The business is demonstrating explosive fundamental momentum with a compounded profit growth of 59% over the trailing twelve months [E15], alongside structural margin expansion that lifted operating margins to 21% in March 2026 compared to just 5% three years earlier [E17]. Balance sheet risk has been aggressively neutralized as borrowings plummeted to Rs 2 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 9 Cr a year earlier, driving the debt-to-equity ratio down to a pristine 0.02x and rendering the firm almost debt-free [E25, E23, E37]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow intrinsic value sits at Rs 199 per share against the current market price of Rs 182, providing a margin of safety while reverse DCF analysis reveals that the market price assumes a mere 8.7% earnings growth against a base case of 10.0% [E31, E33]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -4 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -7 Cr in March 2026 [E21, E22], and debtor days have increased from 94.7 to 149 days [E39].

Despite reported profitability, the company suffers from a severe cash flow disconnect, generating negative operating cash flow of Rs -4 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -7 Cr for Mar 2026, resulting in a troubling cash conversion ratio of -0.22x [E20, E21, E22]. Operating margins exhibit underlying fragility, with the yearly and quarterly trends both flagged as inconsistent [E18, E19]. Working capital management is deteriorating rapidly, evidenced by debtor days ballooning from 94.7 to 149 days [E39]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company stubbornly returns nothing to shareholders, maintaining a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E38]. Conceded: the company boasts an extremely high ROCE of 65.5% alongside minimal debt of Rs 2 Cr [E12, E25].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow were negative at Rs -4 Cr and Rs -7 Cr respectively in Mar 2026, leading to a cash conversion ratio of -0.22x [E20, E21, E22], and debtor days have increased from 94.7 to 149 days [E39]. However, this working capital friction has not hindered extraordinary capital efficiency, where an ROCE of 65.5% [E12] and an ROE of 54.0% [E13] vastly outperform sector medians of 8.4% [E50] and 6.79% [E9]. The bear's concern over inconsistent margin trends [E18, E19] ignores the structural triumph of operating margins expanding by 16 percentage points from 5% three years ago to 21% in Mar 2026 [E17]. While the 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E38] is highlighted as a negative, retaining those earnings directly fuels the company's aggressive debt reduction down to just Rs 2 Cr [E25], leaving borrowings at a remarkably conservative 0.02x of equity [E23]. Furthermore, discounted cash flow modelling proves the stock is currently undervalued at a price of Rs 182 against an intrinsic value of Rs 199 [E31], with a reverse DCF showing the market merely prices in 8.7% growth [E33] against a baseline of 59% compounded profit growth [E15].

Conceded: ROCE stands at 65.5% [E12] and ROE at 54.0% [E13], outperforming sector medians [E9, E50]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash conversion hides a severe underlying strain where operating cash flow was negative at Rs -4 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -7 Cr, producing a cash conversion ratio of -0.22x in Mar 2026 [E20, E21, E22]. This cash drain coincides directly with deteriorating credit collection efficiency, as evidenced by debtor days ballooning from 94.7 to 149 days [E39]. Furthermore, the celebrated 16 percentage point expansion in operating margin to 21% [E17] loses its structural gloss when the yearly and quarterly trends are officially classified as inconsistent over the last two periods [E18, E19]. The bull's defense of a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] as a tool for debt reduction [E25] rings hollow for shareholders who receive zero cash return [E38] while funding an enterprise suffering from negative cash generation [E20]. Finally, relying on a narrow 8.6% margin of safety from a DCF model [E31, E32] offers scant protection when fundamental working capital metrics are moving sharply in the wrong direction [E39].
